gaps.sentence: The ___ (ARRIVE) of the train was announced.
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: arrival (-al noun of 'arrive').

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: The airline is known for its excellent ___ (SERVE).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'excellent'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'serve' is 'service' (-ice); a servant is a person who serves.

gaps.sentence: He is under a lot of ___ at work (PRESS).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'a lot of'; fixed phrase 'under ___'
gaps.explanation: 'Under pressure' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'press' is 'pressure'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INVENT) of the new engine worked day and night.
gaps.explanation: The person who worked day and night is the inventor; 'invention' is the thing created.

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.
